stories.title: 1956. október 23.: A szabadság hajnala
stories.location: Budapest, Bem tér, Kossuth tér és a Bródy Sándor utca
stories.summary: On October 23, 1956, tens of thousands of university students marched in Budapest, carrying national flags with the Stalinist emblem cut out. They gathered at the Bem statue and the Parliament, demanding free elections and Soviet troop withdrawal. By nightfall, the colossal bronze Stalin monument was toppled, and the first shots were fired at the Hungarian Radio.

stories.title: A pesti srácok és a Corvin köz hősei
characters: Pongrátz Gergely, a Corvin köz legendás parancsnoka
stories.location: A Corvin mozi környéke és az Üllői út
stories.summary: Young apprentices, students, and workers—immortalized as the 'boys of Pest'—became the legendary backbone of armed resistance. Stationed at strategic intersections like the Corvin passage and Széna tér, they used homemade Molotov cocktails to destroy dozens of heavily armored Soviet tanks.

stories.title: A győzelem napjai: Nagy Imre és a semlegesség
stories.location: Budapest, Parlament és a Kilián laktanya
stories.summary: Between October 28 and November 3, Hungary tasted true freedom. Prime Minister Imre Nagy formed a democratic coalition government, dissolved the ÁVH, restored the multi-party system, and declared Hungary's perpetual neutrality, renouncing the Warsaw Pact.

stories.title: A Forgószél hadművelet és a segélykiáltás (November 4.)
characters: Nagy Imre, miniszterelnök a mikrofon előtt
stories.location: A Magyar Rádió ideiglenes stúdiója és a csepeli gyártelep
stories.summary: At dawn on November 4, 1956, Soviet forces launched Operation Whirlwind with 2,000 tanks, brutally crushing the revolution. At 5:20 AM, Imre Nagy delivered his immortal radio message to the nation and the world. Despite desperate armed resistance in Csepel and the hills, freedom was overwhelmed by brute force.

stories.title: A kádári megtorlás és a forradalom öröksége
characters: Nyugatra menekülő fiatal mérnök az osztrák határon
stories.location: A budapesti Kozma utcai börtön, az andaui híd és a Hősök tere
stories.summary: Following the defeat, the Moscow-installed puppet regime of János Kádár executed over 350 patriots—including Imre Nagy and Pál Maléter on June 16, 1958—and imprisoned tens of thousands. Over 200,000 Hungarians fled into exile. On June 16, 1989, their historic reburial sealed the collapse of communism, establishing October 23rd as the free Republic's national holiday.

stories.title: Az 1956-os forradalom és szabadságharc története (1956–1989)
characters: Nagy Imre és Maléter Pál mártírok
Pongrátz Gergely és a pesti srácok
Az 1956-os emigráció és az 1989-es rendszerváltó nemzedék
stories.location: Budapest, Bem tér, Corvin köz, Országház és a Hősök tere
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History synthesis of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution: from the student outbreak on October 23rd with the flag with a hole and toppling of Stalin, to the fierce street fighting of the 'boys of Pest' at Corvin köz, Imre Nagy's declaration of neutrality, the crushing Soviet invasion on November 4th, Kádár's brutal retribution, and the triumphant moral resurrection of June 16, 1989.

stories.title: II. Rákóczi Ferenc és a Brezáni kiáltvány
stories.summary: How Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II, the wealthiest landowner in Hungary, answered the call of the peasants and launched the war of independence from Brezán Castle in 1703.

stories.title: A kurucok felkelése és hadviselése
stories.summary: The rapid spread of the Kuruc uprising, light cavalry tactics, the melancholy music of the tárogató, and the liberation of Hungarian territories from the Labanc troops.

stories.title: Az ónodi országgyűlés és a trónfosztás
stories.summary: The dramatic 1707 Diet of Ónód: declaring the dethronement of the Habsburgs, introducing taxation for nobles, copper money inflation, and the turn of military fortune at Trencsén.

stories.title: A szatmári béke és a megbékélés
stories.summary: The 1711 Peace of Szatmár: Count Sándor Károlyi negotiates an honorable compromise that preserves Hungarian constitutional rights and gives general amnesty.

stories.title: Rodostó és a nemzeti emlékezet
stories.summary: Rákóczi's dignified exile in the Turkish town of Rodostó, Kelemen Mikes's famous letters, and how Rákóczi's memory became an eternal pillar of Hungarian patriotism.

stories.title: A Rákóczi-szabadságharc (1703–1711)
stories.summary: The complete historical saga of Rákóczi's War of Independence: from the Brezán proclamation to the Diet of Ónód, the Szatmár compromise, and the immortal exile at Rodostó.

stories.title: A szalámitaktika és a kékcédulás választások (1945–1948)
characters: Rákosi Mátyás, a kommunista párt főtitkára
stories.summary: In 1945, Hungary held free democratic elections in which the Independent Smallholders won 57% of the vote. Backed by Soviet occupation forces, Communist leader Mátyás Rákosi systematically sliced away opposing political parties one by one—a strategy he famously coined 'salami tactics'—culminating in the fraudulent blue-slip elections of 1947.

stories.title: A pártállam és Rákosi személyi kultusza
stories.location: A csepeli Rákosi Mátyás Művek és az iskolai tanterem
stories.summary: By 1949, Hungary was transformed into a totalitarian Stalinist people's republic under the new constitution. Mátyás Rákosi erected a suffocating cult of personality: giant portraits in classrooms and factories, compulsory praise in song and poetry, and total control over every aspect of private and public life.

stories.title: Az ÁVH réme: Andrássy út 60. és a recski tábor
characters: Péter Gábor, az ÁVH rettegett vezetője
stories.location: Budapest, Andrássy út 60. és a recski kőbánya
stories.summary: The cornerstone of Rákosi's totalitarian control was the ÁVH secret police, led by Gábor Péter. Operating out of Andrássy Avenue 60, midnight 'black cars' swept up citizens without trial, deporting bourgeois families to Hortobágy and political dissidents to the brutal secret quarry at Recsk.

stories.title: Koncepciós perek: Rajk László és Mindszenty bíboros
characters: Rajk László, a vádolt egykori belügyminiszter
stories.location: A Markó utcai bíróság díszterme, Budapest
stories.summary: To eliminate every potential rival and intimidate the population, Rákosi staged show trials with pre-scripted verdicts. In 1948, Cardinal József Mindszenty was drugged and sentenced to life imprisonment; in 1949, former interior minister László Rajk was executed as a fabricated 'Titoist spy'.

stories.title: Padlássöprés és a vas országa: Gazdasági zsákutca
stories.summary: Rákosi's economic dogma wreaked havoc on Hungary. In the countryside, 'sweeping the attics' robbed peasants of their last grain to force them into collective farms (téesz). In industry, the regime poured all resources into unviable heavy steel plants ('the country of iron and steel') while food shortages crippled everyday life.

stories.title: A Rákosi-korszak története: Diktatúra, ÁVH-terror és gazdasági összeomlás (1945–1956)
characters: Rákosi Mátyás diktátor és Péter Gábor ÁVH-vezér
Mindszenty József bíboros és Rajk László
A diktatúra üldözöttei: parasztok, polgárok és recski rabok
stories.location: Budapest, Andrássy út 60., Recsk és az Alföld
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History synthesis of post-WWII Hungary under Stalinism: the liquidation of democracy through 'salami tactics' and fraudulent 1947 elections, Mátyás Rákosi's suffocating cult of personality and one-party state, ÁVH secret police terror at Andrássy út 60 and Recsk, fabricated show trials (Rajk, Mindszenty), and agrarian devastation through padlássöprés and heavy industrial dogma.

stories.title: Széchenyi István, a legnagyobb magyar
stories.summary: How Count István Széchenyi offered one year of his income to found the Academy of Sciences and published 'Hitel' (Credit), launching the Reform Era.

stories.title: A Lánchíd és a korszerű modernizáció
stories.summary: The construction of the Chain Bridge linking Buda and Pest, Danube river regulation, steam shipping, and breaking the nobility's ancient tax exemption.

stories.title: Kossuth Lajos és a független politikai sajtó
stories.summary: Lajos Kossuth's courageous journalism: evading Habsburg censorship with handwritten parliamentary reports, editing Pesti Hírlap, and championing serf emancipation.

stories.title: A magyar nyelv diadala és nemzeti jelképei
stories.summary: The landmark 1844 language law making Hungarian the official state language, Kölcsey's Himnusz, Vörösmarty's Szózat, and the founding of the National Theatre.

stories.title: A forradalom küszöbén: a Pilvax és a márciusi ifjak
stories.summary: The electric atmosphere on the eve of March 1848: the Védegylet, young radicals at the Pilvax café, European uprisings, and the threshold of revolution.

stories.title: A reformkor (1825–1848)
stories.summary: The magnificent saga of the Hungarian Reform Era: Széchenyi's foundational vision, the Chain Bridge, Kossuth's political press, the 1844 language act, and the eve of 1848.

stories.title: Az Ellenzéki Kerekasztal és a békés átmenet
characters: Antall József, az Ellenzéki Kerekasztal vezető tárgyalója

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: In September 1987, patriotic writers and dissidents met in Lakitelek, creating the Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF). By March 1989, eight democratic opposition parties and groups formed the Opposition Roundtable (EKA) to face the communist party united. At the National Roundtable talks, they negotiated the bloodless, peaceful transition from single-party rule to a multi-party constitutional democracy.

stories.title: A vasfüggöny lebontása és a határnyitás (1989)
characters: Keletnémet apa a kislányával a zugligeti templomkertben
stories.location: Hegyeshalom, a soproni határszél és a budapesti Zugliget

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: In May 1989, Hungary began physically dismantling the barbed-wire electric fence along the Austrian border. On August 19, the Pan-European Picnic near Sopron allowed hundreds of East Germans to breach the border to the West. Finally, on September 10, 1989, the Hungarian government officially opened the western border, tearing the first brick from the Berlin Wall and uniting Europe.

stories.title: Nagy Imre újratemetése (1989. június 16.)
characters: Orbán Viktor, az ellenzéki ifjúság szónoka
stories.location: Budapest, a Hősök tere és a Rákoskeresztúri új köztemető 301-es parcellája

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: On June 16, 1989, thirty-one years after the execution of Imre Nagy and the martyrs of 1956, over 300,000 Hungarians gathered at Budapest's Heroes' Square. Six coffins stood on the steps of the Műcsarnok, including an empty sixth coffin for all unknown martyrs. The dramatic speech demanding the immediate withdrawal of Soviet troops broke thirty years of silence, marking the moral funeral of the communist system.

stories.title: A Magyar Köztársaság kikiáltása (1989. október 23.)
stories.location: Budapest, a Parlament Kossuth téri erkélye és a tér

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: On October 23, 1989—the 33rd anniversary of the 1956 Revolution—provisional President of the Republic Mátyás Szűrös stepped onto the balcony of the Parliament building overlooking Kossuth Square. Before an exultant crowd of 100,000 citizens, he proclaimed the birth of the free, independent, and democratic Republic of Hungary, consigning the socialist 'People's Republic' to history.

stories.title: Az első szabad választások és az Antall-kormány (1990)
stories.location: Budapest, Országház és egy budapesti szavazóhelyiség

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: In March and April 1990, Hungarians cast their votes in the first free democratic multi-party elections in over four decades. The Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF) won a decisive victory. Historian József Antall formed a center-right coalition government, pledging to serve as 'Prime Minister of 15 million Hungarians in spirit'. The Parliament elected 1956 veteran Árpád Göncz as President, sealing the peaceful birth of the democratic third Republic.

stories.title: A magyar rendszerváltoztatás története (1988–1990)
stories.location: Budapest, Országház, Hősök tere és a soproni határszél

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: A comprehensive historical chronicle of Hungary's negotiated revolution between 1988 and 1990. From the dissident gatherings at Lakitelek and the Opposition Roundtable; the dismantling of the Iron Curtain and the border opening that helped reunify Germany; the cathartic reburial of Imre Nagy on June 16, 1989; the proclamation of the Republic on October 23, 1989; to the first free elections and the inauguration of Prime Minister József Antall and President Árpád Göncz.

stories.title: A tatárok közeledése
stories.summary: In the late 1230s, Friar Julian brought dire news from the East: the unstoppable Mongol armies were advancing toward Europe. King Béla IV attempted to prepare the kingdom and welcomed Cuman refugees, but faced deep suspicion from Hungarian nobles.

stories.title: A muhi csata
stories.summary: On 11 April 1241, the royal army clashed with Batu Khan's forces by the Sajó River at Mohi. Despite initial defense of the bridge, the Mongols outflanked the fortified wagon camp, resulting in a crushing defeat for Hungary.

stories.title: Egy elpusztult ország
stories.summary: Throughout 1241 and 1242, the Mongols laid waste to the country. After the Danube froze in winter, they crossed to Transdanubia, sacking unprotected settlements while King Béla fled all the way to Trau on the Adriatic coast.

stories.title: IV. Béla és az újjáépítés
stories.summary: In spring 1242, the Mongols unexpectedly withdrew. King Béla returned to a ruined kingdom and initiated sweeping reforms: inviting settlers, returning Cumans, and earning the historical title of 'Second Founder of the State'.

stories.title: A kővárak országa
stories.summary: The main lesson of 1241 was that wooden earthworks and open towns burned, while stone castles held out. Béla IV launched a massive fortification campaign, founding Buda Castle and building Visegrád, creating a medieval defense network.

stories.title: The Mongol Invasion (1241–42)
stories.summary: The full historical overview of the Mongol invasion of Hungary in 1241-1242: Julian's warning, the disaster at Mohi, the devastating winter of destruction, Béla IV's flight to Trau, and the king's visionary reconstruction program of stone castles.

stories.title: Buda visszavétele 1686-ban
stories.summary: In the summer of 1686, the multinational Christian army of the Holy League besieged Buda. On September 2, 1686, led by Hungarian hero Dávid Petneházy, allied troops stormed the ramparts, ending 145 years of Ottoman rule in the ancient capital.

stories.title: A győzelmes hadjáratok és a karlócai béke
stories.summary: Following Buda's fall, allied forces crushed the Ottomans at Nagyharsány (1687) and Zenta (1697) under Eugene of Savoy. The 1699 Peace of Karlowitz formally ended Ottoman occupation across virtually all of historic Hungary.

stories.title: A felszabadulás súlyos ára
stories.summary: Liberation came at immense human and material cost: scorched earth, plague epidemics, devastated towns, and crushing military taxes (porció and forspont) imposed by imperial troops quartered across Hungarian villages.

stories.title: Csalódás és elégedetlenség a felszabadulás után
stories.summary: Vienna treated Hungary as a conquered province rather than a liberated partner. The Neoacquistica Commission demanded exorbitant redemption fees from Hungarian nobles, while the Diet of 1687 revoked the hereditary right to elect kings and the right of armed resistance.

stories.title: A kuruc mozgalom és a Rákóczi-szabadságharc hajnala
stories.summary: The smoldering resentment gave birth to the Kuruc insurgent movement. When young Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II answered the call of the peasants in 1703, Hungary launched its greatest struggle for independence under the banner 'Cum Deo pro Patria et Libertate'.

stories.title: A török kiűzése és Magyarország új korszaka (1686–1699)
stories.summary: The dramatic liberation of Hungary from Ottoman rule (1686–1699): the heroic storming of Buda Castle on September 2, 1686 by the Holy League, crushing victories at Nagyharsány and Zenta, the milestone 1699 Peace of Karlowitz, the devastating economic toll of war on common folk, imperial absolutism and noble grievances, and the rise of the Kuruc rebellion under Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II.

stories.title: A békedelegáció Párizsban és Apponyi beszéde
stories.location: Párizs, Neuilly (Château de Madrid), Quai d'Orsay
stories.summary: In January 1920, the Hungarian peace delegation arrives in Paris, confined to the Château de Madrid in Neuilly. On January 16, Count Albert Apponyi delivers his legendary, multilingual defense of Hungary's thousand-year territorial and cultural integrity.

stories.title: 1920. június 4.: A békediktátum aláírása
stories.summary: At 16:32 on June 4, 1920, inside the Grand Trianon Palace at Versailles, two reluctant Hungarian envoys sign the treaty that dismembers the thousand-year-old kingdom. In Budapest, streetcars halt, shops close, and mourning bells toll across the grieving nation.

stories.title: Határon túli magyarság és a kisebbségi sors
stories.summary: Overnight, over three million Hungarians find themselves citizens of foreign successor states without ever leaving their homes. We explore their resilience in Transylvania, Upper Hungary, and the Vojvodina, protecting their native schools, churches, and dual identity.

stories.title: A vagonlakók és a nemzeti trauma
stories.summary: Between 1918 and 1924, nearly 400,000 refugees arrive in truncated Hungary. With housing destroyed or unavailable, entire families live in unheated freight train cars on Budapest railway sidings, fueling the deep interwar trauma and the passionate cry for revision.

stories.title: A Nemzeti Összetartozás Napja: Múltból a jövőbe
stories.location: Budapest, Kossuth tér (Nemzeti Összetartozás Emlékhelye) és Csíksomlyó
stories.summary: A century later, June 4th transforms from a day of bitter grievance into the Day of National Unity. Reflecting modern European values, the Hungarian nation celebrates cultural unity transcending borders, educational ties, and fraternal cooperation in the Carpathian Basin.

stories.title: A trianoni békediktátum és a nemzeti összetartozás (1920–napjainkig)
characters: Gróf Apponyi Albert és Teleki Pál
Benárd Ágost és Drasche-Lázár Alfréd aláírók
A határon túli magyarság és a mai nemzedékek
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History narrative exploring the tragedy and legacy of Trianon: Apponyi's speech in Paris, the signing at Versailles on June 4, 1920, the struggle of transborder Hungarian communities, the refugee crisis, and the modern transformation into the Day of National Unity.

stories.title: 1914: A szarajevói lövés és a háborús láz
stories.summary: In dramatic Rest is History style, we revisit June 28, 1914. Gavrilo Princip's shots in Sarajevo shatter European peace. While Vienna clamors for vengeance, Hungarian Prime Minister István Tisza initially resists the madness, before imperial momentum sweeps the nation into mobilization.

stories.title: Élet a hátországban: jegyrendszer és hadikölcsön
stories.location: Budapest, Nagykörút és a központi vásárcsarnok
stories.summary: The reality of total war strikes civilian life. As the conflict drags on into 1916, Budapest faces severe rationing, shortages of flour and coal, and propaganda urging families to empty their pockets for war bonds while women sustain the city's factories and tramways.

stories.title: Doberdó és az Isonzó pokla
stories.location: Doberdó-fennsík és az Isonzó völgye, Olasz front
stories.summary: On the brutal karst cliffs above the turquoise Isonzo River, Hungarian soldiers endure relentless artillery bombardments in the summer heat and winter ice. A poignant account of the Doberdò plateau, where hundreds of thousands sacrificed their lives.

stories.title: 1918 ősze: Az őszirózsás forradalom
stories.location: Budapest, Astoria Szálló és az Országház tér
stories.summary: October 1918 brings exhaustion and mutiny. As the front collapses, soldiers return to Budapest, ripping off imperial rosettes and pinning autumn asters to their caps. Crowds surge around Hotel Astoria, Károlyi Mihály forms a government, and Hungary declares a republic.

stories.title: A birodalom alkonya és az összeomlás
stories.summary: The euphoria of peace quickly turns to dismay. Instead of Wilsonian self-determination, foreign armies cross the demarcation lines. The historical Kingdom of Hungary fractures as Romanians, Czechs, and Serbs take control of border territories, heralding an epochal turning point.

stories.title: Az első világháború és a történelmi Magyarország összeomlása
characters: Tisza István és Károlyi Mihály miniszterelnökök
Ferenc József és IV. Károly uralkodók
A magyar honvédek és a hátország népe
stories.summary: A gripping Rest is History narrative sweeping through 1914 to 1918: the fatal assassination in Sarajevo, the July crisis, the bloody trenches of Doberdò, the hardships of the home front, the Aster Revolution, and the dramatic collapse of the Dual Monarchy.

stories.title: A Liget Budapest: új múzeumok a városligetben
stories.summary: Adapted and simplified from Wikipedia articles on the Városliget park and the Liget Budapest museum project, for A2 learners.
